findings.title: Deleting a cache does not refresh the displayed cache status
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Since this callback is optional, normal usages without a callback retain the old `cacheUpdatedAt` in the React Query cache after deletion, continue showing the cache as present, and allow repeated deletes that report success even though no cached rows remain. Invalidate or refetch `connectedCalendars` when the mutation settles.

findings.title: Every cache refresh performs an unnecessary update of every selected calendar
findings.body: After repopulating cache entries, this unconditionally runs `updateMany` for all SelectedCalendar rows under the credential solely with an empty data object, thereby advancing their `updatedAt` values. Cache status is now read from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not from SelectedCalendar, so this adds a write and locks all of a credential's selected-calendar rows for every cache refresh (which can be driven frequently by calendar webhooks). It also makes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt no longer represent a selected-calendar change. Remove this update unless there is a consumer that requires this distinct timestamp.

findings.title: The webhook setup script corrupts or fails to update env files on GNU/Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS-specific syntax. On GNU sed, the separate empty argument is interpreted as the sed program rather than an in-place suffix, so the replacement expression is treated as an input filename; the command fails and can leave the target file empty. Because the script does not stop on that failure, it can still print that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated even though it was not. Use platform-aware in-place editing or a portable temporary-file replacement and fail on errors.

findings.title: The new destructive cache-deletion endpoint has no automated authorization coverage
findings.body: No test is added for this handler despite it deleting persisted availability data based on a caller-provided credential ID. Add handler/router tests that verify an owner deletes only rows for their own credential, a different user's credential is rejected without deleting rows, and deleting a credential with no cache is handled as intended. The added shell script only configures a webhook tunnel and does not exercise this endpoint or its ownership boundary.
